clue.text: Corrosive substance in laminate and some coppers

parts.note: Formica is a trade name for a plastic laminate used on worktops
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is a branch of the police

explanation.surface: A chemist finds something corrosive lurking in kitchen worktops and some police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: This acid, found in ant stings, is caustic enough to burn skin.

clue.text: English thus repressing urge for drink

indicators.note: to repress is to hold something down within, so the word for thus encloses the word for urge

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: An English person, holding back an urge, reaches for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong black coffee, forced through by steam, is a common café beverage.

clue.text: Favour topless partner

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter of the word for favour is dropped

parts.note: to espouse a cause is to favour or support it

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about backing a partner who goes without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Naughty or extremely angelic, kept in line

indicators.note: the line's letters hold the pair from angelic within them

parts.note: RY, railway, is a crossword staple for line

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of angelic

explanation.surface: Is someone naughty, or so angelic that they toe the line?
explanation.definitionFit: Racy material is risqué, a little improper or saucy.

clue.text: What driver uses in golf with paper covers

indicators.note: the letters for with and paper wrap around those for in and golf

parts.note: the Mirror is a British daily newspaper
taken as written
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer's driver appears, with a newspaper covering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' tempts a golf club reading; it is a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist checks this side-mounted glass to see traffic behind and alongside.

clue.text: Fix house, a model of patience

parts.note: to put up a guest is to house them
the biblical Job is proverbial for patience

explanation.surface: Fixing up a house calls for saintly patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigged outcome, arranged in advance to deceive, is a fix.

clue.text: Activity of crook detective tails in a restaurant

parts.note: a scam is a swindle, what a crook gets up to
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective trails a crook into a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails' looks like what a detective does to a crook; it is the noun, prawn tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are served under this name on menus.

clue.text: Show contempt with clues written up

indicators.note: in a down entry, written upwards means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: tips are clues or hints

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at clues that have been written up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting at someone is a gesture of scorn.

clue.text: Fare goes down here, so I hope, when flying, to save a grand

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the scrambled letters enclose the pair
flying letters scatter, so so I hope is rearranged

parts.note: G is a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A traveller hopes to save a thousand when flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when flying' turns SOIHOPE into OESOPHI, and 'to save' puts A and G inside it. 'Fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: Food passes down these gullets, the tubes from throat to stomach.

clue.text: International player goes after a French Open

indicators.note: the player's word follows the French one

parts.note: un is French for a
a cap is a player picked for the national side

explanation.surface: An international follows a Frenchman at a tennis Open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' sounds like a tournament but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the lid from a bottle or pen is to open it.

clue.text: Heavenly body which rises when hot

definitions.meaning: the planet closest to the sun
the liquid metal in a thermometer climbs as temperature goes up

explanation.surface: Something in the sky that ascends as it warms.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet and the thermometer metal share one name.

clue.text: He loves to eat more — gut is wobbling

indicators.note: wobbling suggests shaking about, so the letters of more and gut are rearranged

explanation.surface: He wants more food while his gut wobbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastronome is a connoisseur who relishes fine food.

clue.text: Work for policemen including time in station

indicators.note: the word for police work takes the time letter inside it

parts.note: a case is an investigation for the police

explanation.surface: Police work at the station includes the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests a police station; it means rank in society.
explanation.definitionFit: One's station in life is social rank, which a hereditary class system fixes.

clue.text: Cut piece of meat one's ripped off here

parts.note: to clip is to cut
a joint is a roasting cut of meat

explanation.surface: A butcher cuts a joint and gets ripped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar or club that overcharges its customers is this sort of place.

clue.text: Running a bath in bedclothes for housemate

indicators.note: the second half of bedclothes: to clothe is to wrap, so the cot goes round the rest

parts.note: a cot is a small bed; it is the first half of the clue word bedclothes

indicators.note: running water flows freely, so the letters of a bath and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone runs a bath while wrapped in bedclothes, for the housemate.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'bedclothes' does two jobs: split it as 'bed' and 'clothes', a word for a small bed that wraps round the scrambled letters of 'a bath in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a home with another person lives together with them.

clue.text: Flying female monkey call

parts.note: to monkey with something is to tinker with it
to bell is an old word for to call or ring

explanation.surface: A female monkey with a flying call.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's fairy companion flies alongside him to Neverland.

clue.text: What dreams were for Hamlet, with mad hero about to act decisively

indicators.note: the words for mad and hero go around the Hamlet phrase

parts.note: cross means angry, mad
an icon is an idol or hero
Hamlet says of sleep: perchance to dream, ay, there's the rub

explanation.surface: A literary note on Hamlet's dreams and his mad heroics.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'To be or not to be', Hamlet calls the dreams of death the obstacle: 'there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's crossing of that river was an irrevocable commitment, so the idiom means taking a step with no turning back.

clue.text: Sinful lady to abandon sin

parts.note: to shed is to cast off or abandon
evil is wickedness, sin

explanation.surface: A wicked woman resolves to give up sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful or wicked woman is called this, a female demon.

clue.text: Made allowances for Johnny briefly with Kelly?

indicators.note: cut short, the slang word loses its final letter

parts.note: johnny is British slang for a condom
Ned Kelly was an Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: A tale of two people named Johnny and Kelly getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone a fault is to overlook or forgive it.

clue.text: Cut up diamonds with an adherent of Daesh?

parts.note: D is diamonds, the card suit
Daesh is another name for IS, Islamic State, so one of its followers is an IS member

explanation.surface: A jewel thief with terrorist ties cuts up diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack a body limb from limb is to sever it into pieces.

clue.text: Advance needing to be paid? Keep quiet

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a bill that is due must be paid

explanation.surface: A worker asks for a sub on wages and is told to hush.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue a crowd is to calm or quieten it.

clue.text: A little colour for one idiot pirouetting

indicators.note: spinning round makes the words face the other way, so they read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot ballet dancer pirouettes in a dash of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace or hint of colour is a slight shade.

clue.text: He demands a contribution from tenor and American guitarist

parts.note: T is tenor in music
axman is US slang for a guitarist, the guitar being an axe

explanation.surface: A tenor and a guitarist ask for a contribution from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax collector requires everyone to pay into public funds.

clue.text: Door's opening, better frantically peer in here?

indicators.note: the opening of the word door is its first letter
frantic movement scatters the letters of better

explanation.surface: A nosy person frantically peers in through a door's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer in' suggests peeping; a peer is a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: This British reference book lists the nobility and their families, so a lord would appear there.

clue.text: Party, I see, raised capital

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of understanding

explanation.surface: At a party, someone exclaims as the capital is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Qatar.

clue.text: River guide to straighten out fool's garment

parts.note: a cox steers a rowing boat on the river
to comb hair is to untangle it

explanation.surface: A river guide tidies up a jester's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester traditionally wore a cap topped with a red crest like a cock's.

clue.text: 1 under 100 could be 99

indicators.note: in a down entry, the word for one sits below the numeral

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
one is the number 1 in words

explanation.surface: A numerical riddle: one less than 100 makes 99.
explanation.walkthrough: The arithmetic lures; a 99 is a British soft ice cream in a wafer with a chocolate flake.
explanation.definitionFit: The wafer holder of that ice cream is one example of this item.

clue.text: She's very alluring in the first sixty minutes

parts.note: an hour is sixty minutes
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly captivating within the first hour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition these beautiful maidens await the faithful in paradise; the word now means any seductive woman.

clue.text: With no match training, one-nil is about average

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the average
training reshapes something, so the letters of one-nil are rearranged

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

explanation.surface: A football team without match training wins one-nil, an average result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' scrambles one-nil into NONEIL, which 'is about' wraps round the average. 'match' looks like a fixture; it means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrivalled, without equal, is supreme.
